description: The pie chart presents the distribution of sources/outlets referenced in the context of “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” showing a total of 17 slices. The largest slice is labeled “Other” and appears in gray at roughly about one-fifth of the circle (no number is printed inside it), followed by “Breitbart” in blue labeled 14%. Additional slices include “Drudge Report” in orange labeled 8% and “The Daily Caller” in green labeled 8%, “The Huffington Post” in red labeled 7%, “NPR” in purple labeled 6%, “Vox” in brown labeled 6%, “The Guardian” in pink labeled 5%, “BBC” in gray labeled 5%, “RT” in yellow-green labeled 4%, and seven smaller slices each labeled 3%: “Daily Kos” (light blue), “National Review” (teal), “Daily Mail” (orange), “RedState” (green), “Fox News” (red), “CNN” (purple), and “Shareblue PoliticusUSA” (brown/pink-toned). Percentage values are printed inside most slices (except the “Other” slice), there is no separate legend, and no slices appear exploded or otherwise emphasized; the slices are arranged around the circle without an obvious strictly descending order.
